content: 1. Lamivudine (Epivir) is administered at a dose of 300 mg orally once daily or 150 mg orally every 12 hours. For Epivir HBV, the dose is 100 mg orally once daily. 2. For patients with a creatinine clearance (CrCl) ≥ 50 mL/min, the recommended dose is 150 mg orally every 12 hours or 300 mg orally once daily. 3. For patients with CrCl between 30-49 mL/min, the dose is reduced to 150 mg orally once daily. 4. For patients with CrCl between 15-29 mL/min, the initial dose is 150 mg, followed by 100 mg orally once daily. 5. For patients with CrCl between 5-14 mL/min, the initial dose is 150 mg, followed by 50 mg orally once daily. 6. For patients with CrCl < 5 mL/min, the initial dose is 50 mg, followed by 25 mg orally once daily. 7. Lamivudine is used in combination with zidovudine (Combivir), abacavir (Epzicom), or abacavir/zidovudine. 8. Amylase levels should be monitored every 4-8 weeks during treatment. 9. Lamivudine is indicated for the treatment of HIV infection in combination with other antiretroviral agents. 10. The safety and efficacy of Epivir HBV in children under 2 years of age have not been established. For children aged 2 years or older, the recommended dose is 3 mg/kg orally once daily, not exceeding 100 mg/day. 11. The 150-mg scored tablet is the preferred formulation for HIV-1-infected children and adolescents weighing ≥ 14 kg who can tolerate solid dosage forms. 12. Tablet regimens are recommended when possible to avoid potential interactions with sorbitol. 13. When treating with lamivudine oral solution, consider more frequent monitoring of HIV-1 viral load due to potential interactions with sorbitol-containing solutions. 14. Co-administration of lamivudine with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated, as this combination is a complete regimen for HIV and should not be used with other antiretrovirals. 15. Co-administration of emtricitabine-containing products and lamivudine-containing products should be avoided due to the risk of therapeutic duplication and increased risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. 16. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of gene therapy products such as atidarsagene autotemcel, betibeglogene autotemcel, and lovotibeglogene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 17. Sorbitol-containing solutions decrease systemic exposure to lamivudine oral solution, leading to lower rates of virologic suppression, reduced plasma lamivudine levels, and increased viral resistance compared to lamivudine tablets. 18. Tafenoquine increases lamivudine levels by inhibiting organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters. Avoid co-administration or monitor for substrate-related toxicities. 19. Trilaciclib decreases lamivudine levels by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely for toxicities. 20. Co-administration of lamivudine with drugs such as abacavir, atazanavir, efavirenz, enfuvirtide, fosamprenavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, nevirapine, ritonavir, tenofovir DF, and tipranavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lamivudine increases cabozantinib levels by inhibiting MRP2 transporters, which may increase toxicity. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustments. 22. Co-administration of lamivudine with ganciclovir or valganciclovir increases the risk of hematologic toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Ribavirin increases lamivudine toxicity, including the risk of lactic acidosis, through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use alternatives if available and monitor closely. 24. Interferon alfa-2a and alfa-2b increase the risk of liver decompensation when co-administered with lamivudine. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Sulfamethoxazole increases lamivudine levels by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 26. Orlistat decreases lamivudine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to loss of virological control in HIV-infected patients. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 27. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may increase lamivudine levels. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitor closely. 28. Lamivudine and zidovudine exhibit beneficial pharmacodynamic synergism, but both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Givinostat, a weak OAT2 inhibitor, may increase lamivudine levels. Monitor closely if co-administered with OCT2-sensitive substrates. 30. Lamivudine increases erdafitinib levels by decreasing renal clearance. Consider alternatives or reduce the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability.
